questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.1)
questions.stem_en: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes $6\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$ to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in new unit is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes $6\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$ to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in new unit is:
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Time, $t = 6\text{ min } 40\text{ s}$
$= 360 + 40$
$= 400\text{ s}$

Distance in new system $d = vt$
$= 1 \times 400 = 400$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — System of Particles and Rotational Motion (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.4)
questions.stem_en: The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from $600\text{ rpm}$ to $1200\text{ rpm}$ in $10\text{ s}$. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: System of Particles and Rotational Motion] The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from $600\text{ rpm}$ to $1200\text{ rpm}$ in $10\text{ s}$. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\alpha = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{\Delta t} = \left(\frac{1200 - 600}{10}\right)\frac{2\pi}{60} = 2\pi\text{ rad/s}^2$

$\Rightarrow$ Use equation of motion, $\omega_2^2 = \omega_1^2 + 2\alpha\theta$

$\Rightarrow \omega_2 = 1200 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 40\pi$

$\omega_1 = 600 \times \frac{2\pi}{60} = 20\pi$

$(40\pi)^2 = (20\pi)^2 + 2 \times 2\pi\theta$

$\Rightarrow 1200 \pi^2 = 4\pi\theta$

$\Rightarrow \theta = 300\pi\text{ radian}$

$\Rightarrow \text{Number of revolution} = \frac{\theta}{2\pi} = 150$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA NEET 2026 விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் C** (150). பாடம்: System of Particles and Rotational Motion (NCERT Class 11 Physics — System of Particles and Rotational Motion (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.4)).
questions.ncert_key_point: [NEET 2026 Official • Direct NCERT Concept] Official Answer: Option C — System of Particles and Rotational Motion (Class 11).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.7)
questions.stem_en:
A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of $2 : 1$ by mass. The temperature of the mixture is $27^\circ\text{C}$. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases $\left(\frac{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}}}{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}}\right)$ is:

(Atomic mass of argon $= 40.0\text{ u}$ and molecular mass of chlorine $= 70.0\text{ u}$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of $2 : 1$ by mass. The temperature of the mixture is $27^\circ\text{C}$. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases $\left(\frac{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}}}{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}}\right)$ is:

(Atomic mass of argon $= 40.0\text{ u}$ and molecular mass of chlorine $= 70.0\text{ u}$)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $V_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$

For same temperature, $V_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$

$$\frac{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Ar}}}{V_{\text{rms}}^{\text{Cl}}} = \sqrt{\frac{M_{\text{Cl}}}{M_{\text{Ar}}}} = \sqrt{\frac{70}{40}} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA NEET 2026 விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core (NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.7)).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.9)
questions.stem_en:
Match List I with List II.

| | List-I | | List-II |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A. | $E = h\nu$ | I. | de Broglie wavelength |
| B. | Diffraction and Interference | II. | Particle nature of light |
| C. | $\lambda = h/p$ | III. | Wave nature of light |
| D. | Compton effect | IV. | Energy of photon |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter] Match List I with List II.

| | List-I | | List-II |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A. | $E = h\nu$ | I. | de Broglie wavelength |
| B. | Diffraction and Interference | II. | Particle nature of light |
| C. | $\lambda = h/p$ | III. | Wave nature of light |
| D. | Compton effect | IV. | Energy of photon |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.**

A. $E = h\nu$ is energy of photon

B. Diffraction and interference confirm wave nature of light

C. $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$ is de Broglie wavelength of particle.

D. Compton effect confirms particle nature of light.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Work, Energy and Power (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.13)
questions.stem_en: The amount of work done to raise a mass '$m$' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth '$R$' will be
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Work, Energy and Power] The amount of work done to raise a mass '$m$' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth '$R$' will be
questions.explanation_en:
Answer (4)
Sol. W.D. = $U_2 - U_1$

$= -\frac{GMm}{R+R} - \left(-\frac{GMm}{R}\right)$

$= -\frac{GMm}{2R} + \frac{GMm}{R}$

$= \frac{GMm}{2R} = \frac{mgR}{2}$

questions.stem_en: Each side of a metallic cube of mass $5.580\text{ kg}$ is measured to the $9.0\text{ cm}$. Keeping the significant figures in view, the density of the material of the cube can be best expressed as $X \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ where the value of $X$ is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Units and Measurements] Each side of a metallic cube of mass $5.580\text{ kg}$ is measured to the $9.0\text{ cm}$. Keeping the significant figures in view, the density of the material of the cube can be best expressed as $X \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ where the value of $X$ is:
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. Density} = = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Volume}}$

$= \frac{5.580\text{ kg}}{(9.0\text{ cm})^3}$

$= \frac{5.580}{729} \times 10^6 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

$= 0.007654321 \times 10^6 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

$= 7.654 \times 10^3 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

$= 7.7 \times 10^3 \frac{\text{kg}}{\text{m}^3}$

Hence, on comparing

$X = 7.7$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Work, Energy and Power (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.16)
questions.stem_en:
The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is $0.02\text{ joule}$. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately:
(Consider mass of the bob = $20\text{ g}$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Work, Energy and Power] The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is $0.02\text{ joule}$. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately:
(Consider mass of the bob = $20\text{ g}$)
questions.explanation_en:
At equilibrium position

Total energy = K.E

$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.02$

$\frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times v^2 \times 10^{-3} = 2 \times 10^{-2}$

$v = \sqrt{2}$

$v = 1.41\text{ m/s}$

questions.stem_en: In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is $\lambda$, is $K$ units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is $\frac{\lambda}{3}$ will be
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Wave Optics] In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$, the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is $\lambda$, is $K$ units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is $\frac{\lambda}{3}$ will be
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $I = I_0 \cos^2 \frac{\Delta\phi}{2}$ [$I_0 \rightarrow$ maximum intensity]

$I = I_0 \cos^2 \frac{K\Delta x}{2}$

$K = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \frac{\lambda}{2}\right)$

$K = I_0$

$K_1 = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \frac{\lambda}{3 \times 2}\right) = I_0 \cos^2 \left(\frac{\pi}{3}
ight)$

$K_1 = \frac{I_0}{4}$

$\frac{K}{K_1} = 4 \Rightarrow K_1 = \frac{K}{4}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA NEET 2026 விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் A** ($\frac{K}{4}$). பாடம்: Wave Optics (NCERT Class 12 Physics — Wave Optics (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.17)).

In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. If it reduces in one region, producing a dark fringe, it increases in another region, producing a bright fringe.

questions.stem_en:
For a travelling harmonic wave
$y(x, t) = 2.0 \cos 2\pi(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in $\text{cm}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$. The phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of $0.5\text{ m}$ is:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] For a travelling harmonic wave
$y(x, t) = 2.0 \cos 2\pi(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35)$, where $x$ and $y$ are in $\text{cm}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$. The phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of $0.5\text{ m}$ is:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $y(x, t) = 2.0 \cos 2\pi(10t - 0.008x + 0.35)$

Total phase

$\phi = 20\pi - 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3}x + 2\pi \times 0.35$

$\Delta\phi = k\Delta x$

$\Delta\phi = 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3}\ \Delta x$

$= 2\pi \times 8 \times 10^{-3} \times \left(\frac{100}{2}\right)$

$= 8\pi \times 10^{-1} = 0.8\pi$

questions.stem_en: Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance $200\text{ pF}$. One of them is charged by a $100\text{ V}$ supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is:

questions.stem_en: In a vernier calliper, $20\text{ VSD}$ coincide with $16\text{ MSD}$ (each division of length $1\text{ mm}$). The least count of the vernier callipers is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Units and Measurements] In a vernier calliper, $20\text{ VSD}$ coincide with $16\text{ MSD}$ (each division of length $1\text{ mm}$). The least count of the vernier callipers is:
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. Least count of vernier callipers}$
$\text{L.C.} = 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} \quad \dots\text{(i)}$
$20\text{ VSD} = 16\text{ MSD}$
$1\text{ VSD} = \frac{16}{20}\text{ MSD}$
$\text{From (i)}$
$\text{L.C.} = 1\text{ MSD} - \frac{16}{20}\text{ MSD}$
$\text{L.C.} = \frac{4}{20}\text{ MSD}$
$\text{L.C.} = \frac{1}{5}\text{ mm} = 0.2\text{ mm}$
$\text{L.C.} = 0.02\text{ cm}$

When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. ($g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$)

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. ($g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$)

A. Person A has reaction time of 0.20 s.
B. Person B has reaction time of 0.22 s.
C. Person C has reaction time of 0.18 s.
D. Person D has reaction time of 0.19 s.
E. Person E has reaction time of 0.21 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.28)
questions.stem_en: A room heater is rated 400 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately)?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] A room heater is rated 400 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately)?
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Rated power of heater

$P_0 = \frac{V_0^2}{R}$ ...(i)

Consumed power

$P_c = \frac{V^2}{R}$ ...(ii) [$V \rightarrow$ applied voltage]

From (i) and (ii)

$\frac{P_c}{P_0} = \frac{V^2}{V_0^2}$

$P_c = \left[ \frac{V}{V_0} \right]^2 P_0$

$P_c = \left[ \frac{200}{220} \right]^2 \times 400$

$P_c = 331 \text{ W}$

questions.stem_en:
A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of $3.14 \times 10^{-3}$ T at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively :

(Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ T m/A)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Moving Charges and Magnetism] A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of $3.14 \times 10^{-3}$ T at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively :

(Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ T m/A)
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Magnetic field of a circular loop:

$B_0 = \frac{\mu_0 Ni}{2R}$

$$i = \frac{2RB_0}{\mu_0 N} = \frac{2 \times 5 \times 10^{-2} \times 3.14 \times 10^{-3}}{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 100}$$

$i = 2.5 \text{ A}$

Magnetic moment

$M = NiA$

$= 100 \times 2.5 \times 3.14 \times (5 \times 10^{-2})^2\ [\because A = \pi R^2]$

$= 2 \text{ A m}^2$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA NEET 2026 விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் D** (2.5 A, 2 A m$^2$). பாடம்: Moving Charges and Magnetism (NCERT Class 12 Physics — Moving Charges and Magnetism (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.29)).

questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Electromagnetic Induction] A rectangular wire loop of sides $8\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$ with a small cut, is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.3\text{ T}$ directed normal to the plane of the loop. questions.stem_en:
Four statements are given ($A$ is mass number):

A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A^{1/3}$.

B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.

C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect.

D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Nuclei] Four statements are given ($A$ is mass number):

A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A^{1/3}$.

B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to $A$.

C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect.

D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:

choices.text_en: A and C are true, but B and D are false
choices.text_ta: A and C are true, but B and D are false

choices.text_en: B and C are true, but A and D are false
choices.text_ta: B and C are true, but A and D are false

choices.text_en: A and D are true, but B and C are false
choices.text_ta: A and D are true, but B and C are false

choices.text_en: B and D are true, but A and C are false
choices.text_ta: B and D are true, but A and C are false

questions.explanation_en:
As we know,

Size of nucleus, $r = r_0(A)^{\frac{1}{3}}$

$\Rightarrow r^3 = r_0^3 \cdot A$

$\Rightarrow V \propto A \quad \left(\because V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right)$

So, option A $\rightarrow$ wrong and B $\rightarrow$ correct

while the difference between the actual mass of nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect.

$\therefore$ option C $\rightarrow$ wrong and D $\rightarrow$ correct

questions.stem_en: Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum $L$, notes down the data of time taken to complete 30 oscillations as $60\text{ s}$ and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (Take $\pi^2 = 9.8$, and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Oscillations] Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum $L$, notes down the data of time taken to complete 30 oscillations as $60\text{ s}$ and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (Take $\pi^2 = 9.8$, and $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explanation_en:
Time taken for 30 oscillations $= 60\text{ s}$

Time period of simple pendulum = Time taken for 1 oscillation

$\Rightarrow T = \frac{60}{30} = 2\text{ s}$

$$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}} \Rightarrow l = \frac{gT^2}{4\pi^2} = \frac{9.8 \times 2 \times 2}{4 \times 9.8} = 1\text{ m}$$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Thermodynamics (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.34)
questions.stem_en: An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of $100\text{ W}$. If the system performs work at a rate of $75\text{ J/s}$, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Thermodynamics] An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of $100\text{ W}$. If the system performs work at a rate of $75\text{ J/s}$, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be:
questions.explanation_en:
Using $1^{\text{st}}$ law of thermodynamics for electric heater,

$Q = \Delta U + W$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + \frac{dW}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow 100\text{ W} = \frac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} + 75\text{ W}$

$\therefore \frac{d(\Delta U)}{dt} = 25\text{ W}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.38)
questions.stem_en: The peak value of an alternating current is $5\text{ A}$ and frequency is $60\text{ Hz}$. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] The peak value of an alternating current is $5\text{ A}$ and frequency is $60\text{ Hz}$. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value?
questions.explanation_en:
**Answer (4)**

**Sol.** Alternating current,

$i = i_{\text{peak}} \sin(\omega t)$

where $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 60 = 120\pi\text{ rad/s}$

$\Rightarrow i = 5\sin(120\pi t)$

$\Rightarrow 5 = 5\sin(120\pi t)$

$\Rightarrow \sin(120\pi t) = 1 = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$\therefore 120\pi t = \frac{\pi}{2}$

$\Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{240}\text{ s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Electric Charges and Fields (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.41)
questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are correct?

A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.

B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.

C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.

D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.

E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Electric Charges and Fields] Which of the following statements are correct?

A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.

B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.

C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.

D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.

E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
Answer (3)

**Sol.**

A. Electrostatic field is zero inside a conductor.

B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor $= \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0} \hat{n}$, depends on surface charge density ($\sigma$).

C. The interior of a charged conductor cannot have any excess charge in the static situation.

D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field $\perp$ surface.

E. The electrostatic potential is constant and can be non-zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.

questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.42)
questions.stem_en:
For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does ***not*** give rise to the photoelectric effect?
(Take Planck's constant as $6.6 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter] For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does ***not*** give rise to the photoelectric effect?
(Take Planck's constant as $6.6 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. For incident radiation having wavelength ($\lambda$), photoelectric effect doesn't occur when $\frac{hc}{\lambda} \frac{hc}{W_0}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda > \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{6.6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda > \frac{3 \times 10^{-7}}{1.6}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda > \frac{300}{1.6}\text{nm}$

$\Rightarrow \lambda = 187.5\text{ nm}$

$\therefore$ Option (3) 200 nm is correct.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.44)
questions.stem_en:
A submarine is designed to withstand an absolute pressure of $100\text{ atm}$. How deep can it go below the water surface?

(Consider the density of water $= 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$,
$1\text{ atm} = 1 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] A submarine is designed to withstand an absolute pressure of $100\text{ atm}$. How deep can it go below the water surface?

(Consider the density of water $= 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}$,
$1\text{ atm} = 1 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $P = P_0 + \rho g h$

$\Rightarrow 100 \times 10^5 = 10^5 + 10^3 imes 10 \times h$

$\Rightarrow 10^7 = 10^5 + 10^4 h$

$\Rightarrow 10^3 = 10 + h$

$\Rightarrow h = 1000 - 10 = 990\text{ m}$

Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines.

A. (i) $\text{LiAlH}_4$; (ii) $\text{H}_2\text{O}$

B. $\text{Sn} + \text{HCl}$

C. $\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}$

D. $\text{Na(Hg)}/\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry — Chemical Thermodynamics (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.48)
questions.stem_en:
Consider the following reaction :

$\text{2A(g)} + \text{B(g)} \rightarrow \text{2D(g)}$

$$\Delta\text{U}^{\ominus} = -10\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\text{ and }\Delta\text{S}^{\ominus} = -44\text{ JK}^{-1}\text{ at 298 K.}$$

Identify the **correct** option with $\Delta\text{G}^{\ominus}$ for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K.

(Given : $\text{R} = 8.31\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemical Thermodynamics] Consider the following reaction :

$\text{2A(g)} + \text{B(g)} \rightarrow \text{2D(g)}$

$$\Delta\text{U}^{\ominus} = -10\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\text{ and }\Delta\text{S}^{\ominus} = -44\text{ JK}^{-1}\text{ at 298 K.}$$

Identify the **correct** option with $\Delta\text{G}^{\ominus}$ for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K.

(Given : $\text{R} = 8.31\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{2A(g)} + \text{B(g)} \rightarrow \text{2D(g)}$

$\Delta\text{U}^\circ = -10\text{ kJ/mol}$

$\Delta\text{S}^\circ = -44\text{ J/K}$

$\Delta\text{H}^\circ = \Delta\text{U}^\circ + \Delta\text{n}_\text{g}\text{RT}$

$$\Delta\text{H}^\circ = -10 - \frac{1 \times 298 \times (8.31)}{1000} = -10 - 2.48 = -12.48\text{ kJ/mol}$$

$\Delta\text{G}^\circ = \Delta\text{H}^\circ - \text{T}\Delta\text{S}^\circ$

$= -12.48 - \frac{298 \times (-44)}{1000}$

$= -12.48 + 13.112$

$= +0.632\text{ kJ/mol}$

Since $\Delta\text{G}^\circ$ comes out to be positive, so given process is non-spontaneous.

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry — Chemistry NCERT Core (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.50)
questions.stem_en:
In a qualitative analysis, $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ is detected by appearance of precipitate of $\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s})$. Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at $298\text{ K}$.
$$\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}), \text{ K} = 4 \times 10^{-10}$$
(Given : $\log2 = 0.3010$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] In a qualitative analysis, $\text{Bi}^{3+}$ is detected by appearance of precipitate of $\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s})$. Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at $298\text{ K}$.
$$\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{BiO}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}), \text{ K} = 4 \times 10^{-10}$$
(Given : $\log2 = 0.3010$)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \underset{\text{s}}{\text{BiO}^+(\text{aq})} + \underset{\text{s}}{\text{OH}^-(\text{aq})}$

$\text{K} = \frac{[\text{BiO}^+][\text{OH}^-]}{[\text{BiO}(\text{OH})(\text{s})]}$

$\text{K} = \frac{[\text{BiO}^+][\text{OH}^-]}{1}$

$\text{K} = \text{s} \times \text{s} = \text{s}^2$

$\text{s} = \sqrt{\text{K}} = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-10}} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$

$[\text{H}^+] = \frac{\text{K}_\text{w}}{[\text{OH}^-]} = \frac{1}{2} \times 10^{-9}, \text{ pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+] = 9 + \log 2 = 9.301$

questions.stem_en: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% energy into light. If energy of one photon is $4.42 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% energy into light. If energy of one photon is $4.42 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J}$, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second?
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.**

Energy = Power $\times$ time
$= 150\text{ watt} \times 1\text{ s}$
$= 150\text{ J}$

Energy converted to light $= \frac{150 \times 8}{100} = 12\text{ J}$

$E = nh\nu$

Energy of one photon $= 4.42 \times 10^{-19}$

So, $n = \text{number of photons} = \frac{E}{h\nu} = \frac{12}{4.42 \times 10^{-19}}$
$= 2.715 \times 10^{19}$

questions.stem_en: Identify the *incorrect* statement from the following:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Structure of Atom] Identify the *incorrect* statement from the following:

choices.text_en: Nitrogen can form $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself.
choices.text_ta: Nitrogen can form $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself.

choices.text_en: $\text{P}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3$ and $\text{As}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_3$ form $d\pi-d\pi$ bond with transition metals.
choices.text_ta: $\text{P}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3$ and $\text{As}(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_3$ form $d\pi-d\pi$ bond with transition metals.

choices.text_en: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.
choices.text_ta: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.

choices.text_en: Nitrogen can form $d\pi-p\pi$ bond with oxygen.
choices.text_ta: Nitrogen can form $d\pi-p\pi$ bond with oxygen.

questions.explanation_en:
Sol.

* Both nitrogen and oxygen do not contain d-orbitals so it cannot form $d\pi-p\pi$ bond.
* Phosphorus and Arsenic can form $d\pi-d\pi$ bond with transition metals. Since both have vacant d-orbitals by which it can interact with transition metals and can involve in $d\pi-d\pi$ interaction.
* Phosphorous, Arsenic and Antimony show catenation property.

An ambidentate ligand is a ligand which has two different donor atoms and either of the two ligates in complex.

(1) Ethane-1,2-diamine $\rightarrow$ didentate

(2) Ethylenediamine tetraacetate ion $\rightarrow$ hexadentate

(3) Thiocyanate ($\text{SCN}^-$) $\rightarrow$ Ambidentate ligand.

(4) Oxalate $\rightarrow$ didentate

questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Structure of Atom] The correct order of increasing metallic character of $\text{Na}$, $\text{Be}$, $\text{P}$, $\text{Mg}$ and $\text{Si}$ is
questions.explanation_en:
On moving left to right in a period, metallic character decreases and on moving top to bottom in a group, metallic character increases. So, the correct order of increasing metallic character is

$\text{P} < \text{Si} < \text{Be} < \text{Mg} < \text{Na}$

$\text{Electronegativity} \propto \frac{1}{\text{Metallic character}}$

$$\begin{array}{lccccc}
& \textbf{Na} & \textbf{Mg} & \textbf{Be} & \textbf{Si} & \textbf{P} \\
\textbf{Electronegativity (On Pauling scale)} & 0.9 & 1.2 & 1.5 & 1.8 & 2.1
\end{array}$$

(Complex/ion) | | List II

questions.explanation_en:
* In $[\text{Pt}(\text{Cl}_2)(\text{NH}_3)_2]$; $\text{Pt}$ has $dsp^2$ hybridisation, so shape of complex is square planar.

* In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$; $\text{Ni}$ has $sp^3$ hybridisation so shape of complex ion is tetrahedral.
* In $[\text{Fe}(\text{CO})_5]$; shape of complex is trigonal bipyramidal.

questions.stem_en:
Identify the correct statements :
(A) The molality of $2.5\text{ g}$ of ethanoic acid (Molar mass : $60\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $75\text{ g}$ of benzene solution is $0.556\text{ m}$.
(B) The molarity of a solution containing $5\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ (molar mass : $40\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $450\text{ mL}$ of solution is $0.278\text{ M}$ at $298\text{ K}$.
(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water.
(D) The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure.
(E) For a binary mixture of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$, the number of moles of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are $\text{n}_\text{A}$ and $\text{n}_\text{B}$ respectively. The mole fraction of $\text{B}$ will be $\text{x}_\text{B} = \frac{\text{n}_\text{A}}{\text{n}_\text{A} + \text{n}_\text{B}}$.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
(1) A, B and C only
(2) A and B only
(3) A and C only
(4) A, D and E only
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry] Identify the correct statements :
(A) The molality of $2.5\text{ g}$ of ethanoic acid (Molar mass : $60\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $75\text{ g}$ of benzene solution is $0.556\text{ m}$.
(B) The molarity of a solution containing $5\text{ g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ (molar mass : $40\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $450\text{ mL}$ of solution is $0.278\text{ M}$ at $298\text{ K}$.
(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water.
(D) The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure.
(E) For a binary mixture of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$, the number of moles of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are $\text{n}_\text{A}$ and $\text{n}_\text{B}$ respectively. The mole fraction of $\text{B}$ will be $\text{x}_\text{B} = \frac{\text{n}_\text{A}}{\text{n}_\text{A} + \text{n}_\text{B}}$.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
(1) A, B and C only
(2) A and B only
(3) A and C only
(4) A, D and E only
questions.explanation_en:
Sol.

(A) $\text{Molality} = \frac{2.5}{60} \times \frac{1000}{75} = 0.556\text{ molal}$

(B) $\text{Molarity} = \frac{5}{40} \times \frac{1000}{450} = 0.278\text{ M}$

(C) Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water
$\text{Henry's Law } \text{K}_\text{H} \propto \text{Temp} \propto \frac{1}{\text{solubility}}$

(D) According to Henry's Law,
$\text{P} = \text{K}_\text{H}\text{x}$
$\text{P} \propto \text{x}$
$\text{P} \propto \text{Solubility}$
So as $\text{P}\uparrow$, solubility $\uparrow$

(E) $\text{x}_\text{B} = \frac{\text{n}_\text{B}}{\text{n}_\text{A} + \text{n}_\text{B}}$

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is :

(Given : Molar mass of $\text{Cu} = 63\text{ g mol}^{-1}$; $1\text{ F} = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}$)
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{CuSO}_4 \longrightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}$

$2\text{e}^- + \text{Cu}^{2+} \longrightarrow \text{Cu(s)}$

$\text{W} = \text{zit}$

$= \frac{\text{E} \times \text{i} \times \text{t}}{96500}$

$= \frac{63 \times 1.5 \times 10 \times 60}{2 \times 96500}$

$= \frac{56,700}{193000} = 0.2938\text{ g}$

questions.stem_en: At a certain temperature, T (K), during a process, $500\text{ J}$ is absorbed by the system and work of $200\text{ J}$ is done by the system. Then change in internal energy of the system is :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemical Thermodynamics] At a certain temperature, T (K), during a process, $500\text{ J}$ is absorbed by the system and work of $200\text{ J}$ is done by the system. Then change in internal energy of the system is :

$\Delta\text{U} = \text{q} + \text{w}$

$\text{q} = +500\text{ J}$

$\text{w} = -200\text{ J}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry — Equilibrium (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.78)
questions.stem_en:
At $298\text{ K}$, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of $\text{X}^-$ and $\text{HX}$, $\text{K}_\text{b}$ for $\text{X}^-$ is $10^{-10}$.
What is the pH of this buffer solution?

(1) 2
(2) 4
(3) 6
(4) 10
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Equilibrium] At $298\text{ K}$, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of $\text{X}^-$ and $\text{HX}$, $\text{K}_\text{b}$ for $\text{X}^-$ is $10^{-10}$.
What is the pH of this buffer solution?

(1) 2
(2) 4
(3) 6
(4) 10
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{HX} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{X}^-$

$\text{K}_\text{a} \times \text{K}_\text{b} = \text{K}_\text{w}$

$\text{K}_\text{a} = \frac{\text{K}_\text{w}}{\text{K}_\text{b}} = \frac{10^{-14}}{10^{-10}} = 10^{-4}$

$\text{pH} = \text{pK}_\text{a} + \log\frac{[\text{X}^-]}{[\text{HX}]}$

Given that : $[\text{X}^-] = [\text{HX}]$

$= 4 + \log(1)$

$= 4 + 0$

$= 4$

questions.stem_en:
Calculate emf of the half cell given below :
$\text{Pt (s)} \mid \text{H}_2\text{(g, 2 atm)} \mid \text{HCl (aq, 0.02 M)}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^+} = 0\text{ V}$
(Given: $\frac{2.303\text{ RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059$, $\log 2 = 0.3010$)
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] Calculate emf of the half cell given below :
$\text{Pt (s)} \mid \text{H}_2\text{(g, 2 atm)} \mid \text{HCl (aq, 0.02 M)}$
$E^{\circ}_{\text{H}_2/\text{H}^+} = 0\text{ V}$
(Given: $\frac{2.303\text{ RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059$, $\log 2 = 0.3010$)
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{Sol. }\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \longrightarrow 2\text{H}^{\oplus}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^{\ominus}$

$\therefore\text{ E} = \text{E}^{\circ} - \frac{2.303\text{RT}}{\text{nF}}\log \frac{[\text{H}^+]^2}{\text{P}_{\text{H}_2}}$

$[\text{H}^+] = 0.02\text{ M (from HCl)}$

$\text{P}_{\text{H}_2} = 2\text{ atm}$

$\frac{2.303\text{RT}}{\text{F}} = 0.059$

$\text{E} = 0 - \frac{0.059}{2}\log \frac{(0.02)^2}{2}$

$= -0.0295\log\left(\frac{0.0004}{2}\right)$

$\text{E} = -0.0295\log(2 \times 10^{-4})$

$= -0.0295 (\log 2 + \log 10^{-4})$

$= -0.0295 [0.301 - 4] = 0.109\text{ V}$

questions.stem_en: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $\text{Ti}^{2+}\text{ (3d}^2\text{)}$ is :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Structure of Atom] The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of $\text{Ti}^{2+}\text{ (3d}^2\text{)}$ is :

$\text{Sol. Spin only magnetic moment } \mu = \sqrt{\text{n(n} + 2\text{)}}\text{ B.M}$

$\text{n = Number of unpaired e}^-\text{(s)}$

$\text{Electronic configuration of }\text{Ti}^{2+} \Rightarrow \text{[Ar]4s}^0\text{3d}^2$

$\mu = \sqrt{2 \times 4}$

questions.stem_en: When $1\text{ dm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas is passed over hot coke the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes $1.4\text{ dm}^3$. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] When $1\text{ dm}^3$ of $\text{CO}_2$ gas is passed over hot coke the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes $1.4\text{ dm}^3$. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is:
questions.explanation_en:
$\text{CO}_2 + \text{C(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{CO}$
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & & \\
1-x & & 2x
\end{array}$$
$1 - x + 2x = 1 + x = 1.4$
$x = 0.4\text{ dm}^3$
Volume of $\text{CO}_2 = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6\text{ dm}^3$
Volume of $\text{CO} = 2 \times 0.4 = 0.8\text{ dm}^3$

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.

*Pinus* is a gymnosperm.

questions.stem_en:
$2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{ O}_2 \rightarrow 102\text{ CO}_2 + 98\text{ H}_2\text{O} + \text{energy}$

The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule used for respiration, as per the above equation would be :
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Botany: Respiration in Plants] $2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{ O}_2 \rightarrow 102\text{ CO}_2 + 98\text{ H}_2\text{O} + \text{energy}$

The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule used for respiration, as per the above equation would be :
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $\text{R.Q} = \frac{\text{Volume of CO}_2\text{ evolved}}{\text{Volume of O}_2\text{ consumed}}$

As per the given equation,

$2(\text{C}_{51}\text{H}_{98}\text{O}_6) + 145\text{ O}_2 \rightarrow 102\text{ CO}_2 + 98\text{ H}_2\text{O} + \text{Energy}$

Hence the RQ can be calculated as,

$\text{R.Q} = \frac{102}{145} = 0.7$

This value lies between 0.5 and 0.95.

Arrange the following steps of DNA fingerprinting in a correct sequence.

A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonucleases.

B. Hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe.

C. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes.

D. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography.

E. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis.

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Botany: Plant Biology & Genetics] Arrange the following steps of DNA fingerprinting in a correct sequence.

B. Hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe.

C. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes.

D. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography.

E. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation_en:
The following is the correct sequence of steps of DNA fingerprinting.

A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonuclease.

B. Probes made complementary to the VNTR locus are allowed to hybridise with the DNA fragments.

C. The separated DNA fragments are transferred to synthetic membranes made of nylon or nitrocellulose.

D. Finally, the hybridised DNA fragments are detected under X-rays in a technique called autoradiography.

E. DNA fragments are separated based on their size by the technique of gel electrophoresis.

Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence.

B. Isolation of naked protoplasts.

questions.stem_ta:

D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieites of plants.
E. Growing of hybrid protoplast to form a new plant.

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Scientist have even isolated single cell protoplasts from two different varieties of plants each having a desirable character and after digesting their cell walls have been able to isolate naked protoplasts (surrounded by plasma membrane) that can be fused to get hybrid protoplast, which can be further grown to form a new plant. These hybrids are called somatic hybrids, while the process is called somatic hybridization.

So the correct sequence for the formation of somatic hybrids is D, A, B, C, E.

questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are **not** true regarding restriction endonucleases?

A. They are called molecular scissors.
B. These are the enzymes responsible for restricting the growth of bacteriophages in *E. coli*.
C. They cut the DNA only at the centre of the palindromic sites.
D. They remove nucleotides only from the ends of DNA fragments.
E. They recognise specific palindromic base-pair sequences.

Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes] Which of the following statements are **not** true regarding restriction endonucleases?

A. They are called molecular scissors.
B. These are the enzymes responsible for restricting the growth of bacteriophages in *E. coli*.
C. They cut the DNA only at the centre of the palindromic sites.
D. They remove nucleotides only from the ends of DNA fragments.
E. They recognise specific palindromic base-pair sequences.

Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation_en: Sol. Statements C and D are incorrect. Restriction endonucleases usually cut the DNA slightly away from the centre of palindrome sites. They cannot remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA fragment, which is function of restriction exonuclease.

B. Sporogenous tissue
C. Pollen grains
D. Pollen mother cells

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Botany: Cell Cycle and Cell Division] Arrange the following in the correct developmental sequence related to microsporogenesis :
A. Microspore tetrads
B. Sporogenous tissue
C. Pollen grains
D. Pollen mother cells

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. The process of formation of microspores from a pollen mother cell (PMC) through meiosis is called microsporogenesis.

Sporogenous tissue (B) $\rightarrow$ Pollen mother cell (D) $\rightarrow$ Microspore tetrads (A) $\rightarrow$ Pollen grains (C)

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Zoology — Biotechnology: Principles and Processes (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.134)
questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are correct with respect to DNA separation, isolation and visualization?

A. The cutting of DNA is done by molecular scissors.

B. The DNA fragments separate according to their size in an agarose gel, upon electrophoresis.

C. The separated DNA fragments can be seen without staining when exposed to UV light.

D. The separated DNA fragments, when stained with ethidium bromide, can be seen in visible light.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes] Which of the following statements are correct with respect to DNA separation, isolation and visualization?

A. The cutting of DNA is done by molecular scissors.

B. The DNA fragments separate according to their size in an agarose gel, upon electrophoresis.

C. The separated DNA fragments can be seen without staining when exposed to UV light.

D. The separated DNA fragments, when stained with ethidium bromide, can be seen in visible light.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation_en:
* The cutting of DNA is possible by the use of restriction enzymes that results in the fragments of DNA. These fragments of DNA can be separated by a technique known as gel electrophoresis.

* The DNA fragments separate (resolve) according to their size through sieving effect provided by the agarose gel.

* The separated DNA fragments can be visualised only after staining the DNA with a compound known as ethidium bromide followed by exposure to UV radiation.

| B. | Aldosterone | II. | Produces anti-inflammatory reactions |

| D. | Progesterone | IV. | Stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice |

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Chemical Coordination and Integration] Match List I with List II:

| | List-I | | List-II |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A. | Cortisol | I. | Stimulates the formation of alveoli in mammary glands |
| B. | Aldosterone | II. | Produces anti-inflammatory reactions |
| C. | Cholecystokinin | III. | Stimulates reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water from renal tubule |
| D. | Progesterone | IV. | Stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice |

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.**

* Cortisol produces anti-inflammatory reactions and suppresses the immune response.
* Aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water and excretion of $\text{K}^+$ and phosphate ions.
* Cholecystokinin (CCK) acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively.
* Progesterone acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli.

questions.stem_en:
Arrange the following events occuring in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism in the correct order:

A. Increase in blood pressure and Glomerular filtration rate
B. Reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water from distal parts of tubule due to Aldosterone
C. Fall in Glomerular filtration rate
D. Vasoconstriction by Angiotensin II and release of Aldosterone.
E. Renin converts Angiotensinogen into Angiotensin I, followed by Angiotensin II.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Excretory Products and their Elimination] Arrange the following events occuring in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism in the correct order:

A. Increase in blood pressure and Glomerular filtration rate
B. Reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and water from distal parts of tubule due to Aldosterone
C. Fall in Glomerular filtration rate
D. Vasoconstriction by Angiotensin II and release of Aldosterone.
E. Renin converts Angiotensinogen into Angiotensin I, followed by Angiotensin II.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** The JGA plays a complex regulatory role

* A fall in glomerular blood flow/GFR can activate the JG cells to release renin which converts angiotensinogen in blood to angiotensin I and further to angiotensin II
* Angiotensin II, being a powerful vasoconstrictor, increases the glomerular blood pressure and thereby GFR.
* Angiotensin II activates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone.
* Aldosterone causes reabsorption of $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ from the distal parts of the tubule. This leads to an increase in blood pressure and GFR.

questions.stem_en:
In humans, respiration occurs in the following steps. Arrange these steps in the correct order.
A. Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
B. Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ across alveolar membrane
C. Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\text{CO}_2$ rich alveolar air is released out
D. Cellular respiration
E. Transport of gases by the blood
Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Botany: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants] In humans, respiration occurs in the following steps. Arrange these steps in the correct order.
A. Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
B. Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ across alveolar membrane
C. Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\text{CO}_2$ rich alveolar air is released out
D. Cellular respiration
E. Transport of gases by the blood
Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Respiration involves the following steps:
(i) Breathing or pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and $\text{CO}_2$ rich alveolar air is released out.
(ii) Diffusion of gases across alveolar membrane.
(iii) Transport of gases by the blood
(iv) Diffusion of $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2$ between blood and tissues
(v) Utilisation of $\text{O}_2$ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of $\text{CO}_2$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Zoology — Human Health and Disease (NEET 2026 Code 11, Q.139)
questions.stem_en:
The following are the stages of life cycle of *Plasmodium*. Arrange the stages in the proper order.
A. The parasites reproduce asexually in RBCs, bursting the cells.
B. The parasites reproduce asexually in liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing into blood.
C. Gametocytes develop in RBCs.
D. Sporozoites reach the liver through the blood.
E. Female mosquito injects sporozoites into humans during bite.
Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Human Health and Disease] The following are the stages of life cycle of *Plasmodium*. Arrange the stages in the proper order.
A. The parasites reproduce asexually in RBCs, bursting the cells.
B. The parasites reproduce asexually in liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing into blood.
C. Gametocytes develop in RBCs.
D. Sporozoites reach the liver through the blood.
E. Female mosquito injects sporozoites into humans during bite.
Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. *Plasmodium* enters the human body as sporozoites through the bite of an infected female *Anopheles* mosquito. The parasites initially multiply asexually within the liver cells and then attack the RBCs resulting in their rupture.

* Sexual stages (gametocytes) develop in red blood cells.
* When a female *Anopheles* mosquito bites an infected person, these parasites enter the mosquito's body and undergo further development.

B. Ectoparasitic; as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth.

C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but 7 pairs of gill slits were present.

A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage.

B. Ectoparasitic; as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth.

C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but 7 pairs of gill slits were present.

Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters?
questions.explanation_en:
**Answer (2)**

**Sol.** *Petromyzon* sp. have cartilaginous endoskeleton. They have circular sucking mouth. They are ectoparasites on some fishes. Their body is devoid of scales and paired fins. They have 7 pairs (6-15 pairs) of gill slits.

*Scoliodon* and *Exocoetus* are not parasites.

questions.stem_en: The WBC count of a person's blood sample is $8000/\text{cu mm}$. How many eosinophils and lymphocytes would be in the same blood sample approximately?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Body Fluids and Circulation] The WBC count of a person's blood sample is $8000/\text{cu mm}$. How many eosinophils and lymphocytes would be in the same blood sample approximately?
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Eosinophils constitute 2-3% of total WBCs. Hence its value is approximately 2 to 3% of $8000/\text{cu mm} = 160 – 240/\text{cu mm}$ 
Lymphocytes constitute 20-25% of total WBCs. Hence its value is approximately 20 to 25% of $8000/\text{cu mm} = 1600 – 2000/\text{cu mm}$

Select the **incorrect** statements from the following:
A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete.
B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms.

E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Animal Kingdom] Select the **incorrect** statements from the following:
A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete.
B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms.
C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes.
D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes.
E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.
Choose the answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. (A) $\rightarrow$ correct $\rightarrow$ Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system.
(B) $\rightarrow$ incorrect $\rightarrow$ Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of larvae of echinoderms. In adult echinoderms, radial symmetry is seen.
(C) $\rightarrow$ correct $\rightarrow$ Aschelminthes are characterised by the presence of pseudocoelom.
(D) $\rightarrow$ correct $\rightarrow$ Notochord is persistent throughout life in the Chondrichthyes.
(E) $\rightarrow$ incorrect $\rightarrow$ Reptiles are cold-blooded organisms and thus, they cannot maintain a constant body temperature.
Warm-blooded organisms like birds and mammals can maintain a constant body temperature.
Thus, as the incorrect statements are indicated by (B) and (E) only

questions.stem_en: Which of the following equations depicts Verhulst-Pearl logistic population growth?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Botany: Organisms and Populations] Which of the following equations depicts Verhulst-Pearl logistic population growth?
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Verhulst-Pearl logistic population growth is depicted by the equation $\frac{\text{dN}}{\text{dt}} = \text{rN}\left(\frac{\text{K} - \text{N}}{\text{K}}\right)$

Where
- $\text{K}$ = Carrying capacity
- $\text{r}$ = Intrinsic rate of natural increase
- $\text{N}$ = Population density at time 't'

Select the **incorrect** statement with reference to Rh grouping.
A. Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition observed having foetus with $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ blood and mother with $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ blood.
B. Rh antigen is observed on RBCs in the majority of human beings.
C. Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched.
D. Rh incompatibility is observed when a pregnant mother is $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$.
E. Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the second child.

Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Animal & Human Biology] Select the **incorrect** statement with reference to Rh grouping.
A. Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition observed having foetus with $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ blood and mother with $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ blood.
B. Rh antigen is observed on RBCs in the majority of human beings.
C. Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched.
D. Rh incompatibility is observed when a pregnant mother is $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$.
E. Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the second child.

Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation_en:
Sol.
(A) Incorrect $\rightarrow$ A special case of Rh incompatibility has been observed between the $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ blood of a pregnant mother with $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$ blood of the foetus.
(B) Correct $\rightarrow$ Rh antigen is observed on the surface of RBCs of majority (nearly 80 percent) of humans.
(C) Correct $\rightarrow$ Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched to avoid severe problems of destruction of RBCs.
(D) Correct $\rightarrow$ Rh incompatibility (Erythroblastosis foetalis) is observed when a pregnant mother is $\text{Rh}^{-\text{ve}}$ and the foetus is $\text{Rh}^{+\text{ve}}$.
(E) Incorrect $\rightarrow$ Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

Thus, the incorrect statements are (A) and (E).

questions.stem_en:
Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction.

A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre.
B. The neural signal generates an action potential which causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ into sarcoplasm.
C. Increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges.
D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge.
E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Locomotion and Movement] Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction.

A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre.
B. The neural signal generates an action potential which causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ into sarcoplasm.
C. Increase in $\text{Ca}^{++}$ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges.
D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge.
E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :

choices.text_en: A, B, D and E only
choices.text_ta: A, B, D and E only

questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Statements A, B, D and E are correct while statement C is incorrect.

A neural signal reaching neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (Acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This spreads through muscle fibre and causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ into the sarcoplasm. This $\text{Ca}^{++}$ binds to the subunit of troponin on actin filaments and thereby remove the masking of active site for myosin on actin and hence facilitates the formation of cross bridge.

questions.stem_en:
Which of the following statements are correct with reference to human endoskeleton?

A. Human skull is monocondylic.
B. The joint between any two adjoining vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint.
C. In human beings, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven.
D. All ribs except the last 2 pairs are bicephalic.
E. The occipital bone of skull is articulated with atlas vertebra.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Locomotion and Movement] Which of the following statements are correct with reference to human endoskeleton?

A. Human skull is monocondylic.
B. The joint between any two adjoining vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint.
C. In human beings, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven.
D. All ribs except the last 2 pairs are bicephalic.
E. The occipital bone of skull is articulated with atlas vertebra.

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. (A) Incorrect : Human skull is dicondylic. The skull region articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column (Atlas) with the help of two occipital condyles.

(B) Correct : The joint present between the adjacent vertebrae of vertebral column is cartilaginous joints.

(C) Correct : There are 7 cervical vertebrae in human beings.

(D) Incorrect : All ribs of humans are bicephalic, *i.e.*, they have two articulation surfaces on their dorsal end.

(E) Correct : The occipital bone of the skull articultes with the atlas vertebra *via* occipital condyles, forming the atlanto-occiptal joint.

questions.stem_en:
Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions statements to produce sperms. Select the correct from the following :
A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division.
B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes.
C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids.
D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis.
E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Botany: Plant Biology & Genetics] Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions statements to produce sperms. Select the correct from the following :
A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division.
B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes.
C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids.
D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis.
E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. (A) Incorrect : Spermatogonia undergo mitotic differentiation.
(B) Incorrect : Primary spermatocytes undergo 1$^{st}$ meiotic division to form secondary spermatocytes.
(C) Correct : Secondary spermatocytes undergo 2$^{nd}$ meiotic division to form the haploid spermatids.
(D) Incorrect : Spermatids form spermatozoa through a differentiation process called spermiogenesis.
(E) Correct : Spermatids produce spermatozoa via spermiogenesis.
Thus, the correct statements are (C) and (E) only.

questions.explanation_en:

* By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester) of pregnancy, most of the major organ system are formed. The limbs and external genital organs are also well developed.

* By the end of about 24 weeks (ends of second trimester) of pregnancy, the body is covered with fine hair, eye lids separate and eyelashes are formed.

questions.stem_en: The toxin proteins isolated from *Bacillus thuringiensis*, coded by which of the following genes would contrl cotton bollworms and corn borer, respectively?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2026 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Zoology: Biotechnology and its Applications] The toxin proteins isolated from *Bacillus thuringiensis*, coded by which of the following genes would contrl cotton bollworms and corn borer, respectively?
questions.explanation_en: Sol. Specific Bt toxin genes were isolated from *Bacillus thuringiensis* and incorporated into the several crop plants such as cotton. The choice of genes depends upon the crop and the targeted pest, as most Bt toxins are insect-group specific. The toxin is coded by a gene named *cry*. The proteins encoded by the genes *cryIAc* and *cryIIAb* control the cotton bollworms, that of *cryIAb* controls corn borer. questions.stem_en: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length ($L$) and same angle of inclination $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes $2$ times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction ($\mu_k$) between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Laws of Motion] There are two inclined surfaces of equal length ($L$) and same angle of inclination $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes $2$ times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction ($\mu_k$) between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.explanation_en:
$t_{\text{rough}} = 2t_{\text{smooth}}$

$a_{\text{smooth}} = g\sin\theta$

$t \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{a}} \Rightarrow t_{\text{smooth}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{g\sin\theta}}$

$a_{\text{rough}} = g\sin\theta - \mu_k g\cos\theta$

$\frac{t_{\text{rough}}}{t_{\text{smooth}}} = \frac{\sqrt{\sin\theta}}{\sqrt{\sin\theta - \mu_k \cos\theta}} = 2$

Squaring both sides

questions.subject: Physics
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.5)
questions.stem_en: The kinetic energies of two similar cars $A$ and $B$ are $100\text{ J}$ and $225\text{ J}$ respectively. On applying breaks, car $A$ stops after $1000\text{ m}$ and car $B$ stops after $1500\text{ m}$. If $F_A$ and $F_B$ are the forces applied by the breaks on cars $A$ and $B$ respectively, then the ratio of $\frac{F_A}{F_B}$ is
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] The kinetic energies of two similar cars $A$ and $B$ are $100\text{ J}$ and $225\text{ J}$ respectively. On applying breaks, car $A$ stops after $1000\text{ m}$ and car $B$ stops after $1500\text{ m}$. If $F_A$ and $F_B$ are the forces applied by the breaks on cars $A$ and $B$ respectively, then the ratio of $\frac{F_A}{F_B}$ is
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. By work-energy theorem,

$FS = \Delta K\cdot E$

$\Rightarrow -FS = k_f - k_i$

$\Rightarrow FS = k_i - k_f$

$\Rightarrow \frac{F_A}{F_B} = \frac{k_A}{k_B} \times \frac{S_B}{S_A}$

$= \frac{100}{225} \times \frac{1500}{1000}$

$= \frac{150}{225} = \frac{2}{3}$

The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by
$E_z = 60 \cos (5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)$ V/m.

Then expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field) :
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Electromagnetic Waves] The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by
$E_z = 60 \cos (5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)$ V/m.

Then expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field) :
questions.explanation_en:
In electromagnetic wave, $E$ and $B$ are in same phase and $B_0 = \frac{E_0}{c}$; their planes are perpendicular to each other.

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore B_y &= \frac{60}{c} \cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)\text{ T} \\\ &= \frac{60}{3 \times 10^8} \cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)\text{ T} \\\ B_y &= 2 \times 10^{-7} \cos(5x + 1.5 \times 10^9 t)\text{ T} \end{aligned}$$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — System of Particles and Rotational Motion (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.17)
questions.stem_en: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: System of Particles and Rotational Motion] The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
questions.explanation_en:
Assuming the Sun to be a solid sphere, $I = \frac{2}{5}mR^2$

Using conservation of angular momentum, $I'\omega' = I\omega$
$\Rightarrow \frac{2}{5}m(2R)^2 \times \frac{2\pi}{T'} = \frac{2}{5}mR^2 \times \frac{2\pi}{T}$
$\Rightarrow T' = 4T = 4 \times 27 = 108\text{ days}$

According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be ($m$ is the mass of the electron)
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Moving Charges and Magnetism] A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field $B$ states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is $n(h/e)$ where $n$ is an integer, $h$ is Planck's constant and $e$ is the magnitude of electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be ($m$ is the mass of the electron)
questions.explanation_en:
Magnetic force $= \frac{mv^2}{r}$

$evB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$

$v = \frac{eBr}{m}$

$\phi = BA$

$\frac{nh}{e} = B\pi r^2$

$Br^2 = \frac{nh}{e\pi}$

$\mu = IA$

$= \frac{e}{T} \pi r^2$

$= \frac{e \times v}{2\pi r} \pi r^2$

$\mu = \frac{evr}{2}$

$= \frac{1}{2} e \times \frac{eBr}{m} r$

$\mu = \frac{1}{2} e^2 \frac{Br^2}{m}$

$\mu = \frac{1}{2} e^2 \frac{nh}{e\pi m}$

$\mu = \frac{neh}{2\pi m}$

for $n = 1$

$\mu = \frac{eh}{2\pi m}$

questions.stem_en:
A balloon is made of a material of surface tension $S$ and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area $A$. It is filled with a gas of density $
ho$and takes a spherical shape of radius$R$. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius$r$changes from$R$to 0 (zero) in time$T$. If the speed$v(r)$of gas coming out of the balloon depends on$r$as$r^a$and$T \propto S^{\alpha} A^{\beta} \rho^{\gamma} R^{\delta}$ then
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Mechanical Properties of Fluids] A balloon is made of a material of surface tension $S$ and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area $A$. It is filled with a gas of density $
ho$and takes a spherical shape of radius$R$. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius$r$changes from$R$to 0 (zero) in time$T$. If the speed$v(r)$of gas coming out of the balloon depends on$r$as$r^a$and$T \propto S^{\alpha} A^{\beta} \rho^{\gamma} R^{\delta}$ then
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $T \propto S^{\alpha} A^{\beta} \rho^{\gamma} R^{\delta}$

$\mathrm{M}^0\mathrm{L}^0\mathrm{T}^1 = K(\mathrm{MT}^{-2})^{\alpha} (\mathrm{L}^2)^{\beta} (\mathrm{ML}^{-3})^{\gamma} \mathrm{L}^{\delta}$

$\mathrm{M}^0\mathrm{L}^0\mathrm{T}^1 = K[\mathrm{M}^{\alpha + \gamma} \mathrm{L}^{2\beta - 3\gamma + \delta} \mathrm{T}^{-2\alpha}]$

$-2\alpha = 1 \implies \alpha = -\frac{1}{2}$

$\alpha + \gamma = 0 \implies \gamma = \frac{1}{2}$

$2\beta - 3\gamma + \delta = 0$

$2\beta - 3\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + \delta = 0$

By hit and trial (using option (1))

Put $\beta = -1$

$2(-1) - \frac{3}{2} + \delta = 0 \quad \therefore \delta = \frac{7}{2}$

Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at $x = 0.1$ cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed.

questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Units and Measurements] Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Zero error $= +0.1\text{ cm}$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Gravitation (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.31)
questions.stem_en: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury?
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Gravitation] The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury?
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Applying Kepler's $3^{\text{rd}}$ law : $T^2 \propto R^3$
Radius of Martian orbit, $R' = 4R$
$\left(\frac{T'}{T}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{R'}{R}\right)^3 = \left(\frac{4R}{R}\right)^3 = 4^3 = 64 \Rightarrow \frac{T'}{T} = 8$
$\therefore$ Length of 1 year on Mercury = $T = \frac{T'}{8} = \frac{687}{8} = 85.88$ days

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.32)
questions.stem_en: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Physics NCERT Core] A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. $W = mg$ and $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$, $g_h = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{W_h}{W} = \frac{m g_h}{m g} = \frac{g_h}{g} = \frac{R^2}{(R+h)^2}$ $\left(h = \frac{R}{3}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{W_h}{W} = \frac{R^2}{\left(R + \frac{R}{3}\right)^2} = \frac{R^2}{\left(\frac{4R}{3}\right)^2} = \frac{9}{16}$
$\Rightarrow W_h = \frac{9}{16}W = \frac{9}{16} \times 48\quad [W = 48\text{ N}]$
$= 27\text{ N}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA NEET 2025 விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** (27 N). பாடம்: Physics NCERT Core (NCERT Class 12 Physics — Physics NCERT Core (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.32)).

questions.stem_en: An electric dipole with dipole moment $5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Cm}$ is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude $4 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}$. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of $60^\circ$ with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is:
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Electric Charges and Fields] An electric dipole with dipole moment $5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ Cm}$ is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude $4 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}$. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of $60^\circ$ with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is:
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Given

$|\vec{p}| = 5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ C m}$

$|\vec{E}| = 4 \times 10^5\text{ N/C}$

$\theta_i = 0^\circ$ and $\theta_f = 60^\circ$

$\Delta U = U_f - U_i$

$= - PE\cos\theta_f + PE\cos\theta_i$

$= PE[\cos\theta_i - \cos\theta_f]$

$= 5 \times 10^{-6} \times 4 \times 10^5 \left[1 - \frac{1}{2}\right]$

$= 10 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^5 = 1\text{ J}$

questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics — Thermodynamics (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.41)
questions.stem_en: Two gases $A$ and $B$ are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius $r_A$ and $r_B$, respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas $A$ and $B$ are displaced by $16\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio $\frac{r_A}{r_B}$ is equal to
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Thermodynamics] Two gases $A$ and $B$ are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius $r_A$ and $r_B$, respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas $A$ and $B$ are displaced by $16\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio $\frac{r_A}{r_B}$ is equal to
questions.explanation_en:
Using first law of thermodynamics

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + P\Delta V$

$\Delta Q$ is same

$\Delta U$ is also same

$W_A = W_B$

$\therefore (P\Delta V)_A = (P\Delta V)_B$

$P$ is also same

$\dots A_A d_A = A_B d_B$

$\pi r_A^2 d_A = \pi r_B^2 d_B$

$$\frac{r_A}{r_B} = \left(\frac{d_B}{d_A}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} = \left(\frac{9}{16}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$$

$= \frac{3}{4}$
questions.explanation_ta: அதிகாரப்பூர்வ NTA NEET 2025 விடைக்குறிப்பு: **விருப்பம் B** ($\frac{3}{4}$). பாடம்: Thermodynamics (NCERT Class 11 Physics — Thermodynamics (NEET 2025 Code 45, Q.41)).

questions.stem_en:
A physical quantity $P$ is related to four observations $a, b, c$ and $d$ as follows:

$P = a^3 b^2 / c\sqrt{d}$

The percentage errors of measurement in $a, b, c$ and $d$ are 1%, 3%, 2%, and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity $P$ is
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Units and Measurements] A physical quantity $P$ is related to four observations $a, b, c$ and $d$ as follows:

$P = a^3 b^2 / c\sqrt{d}$

The percentage errors of measurement in $a, b, c$ and $d$ are 1%, 3%, 2%, and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity $P$ is
questions.explanation_en:
Sol. Maximum % error in $P = \frac{\Delta P}{P} \times 100 = 3\left(\frac{\Delta a}{a} \times 100\right) + 2\left(\frac{\Delta b}{b} \times 100\right) + \left(\frac{\Delta c}{c} \times 100\right) + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\Delta d}{d} \times 100\right)$

$= 3 \times (1) + 2 \times (3) + (2) + \frac{1}{2} \times (4)$

$= 13\%$

questions.stem_en: Two identical point masses $P$ and $Q$, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants $k_1$ and $k_2$, respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio $(A_Q/A_P)$ of the amplitude $A_Q$ of mass $Q$ to the amplitude $A_P$ of mass $P$ is
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Physics: Oscillations] Two identical point masses $P$ and $Q$, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants $k_1$ and $k_2$, respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio $(A_Q/A_P)$ of the amplitude $A_Q$ of mass $Q$ to the amplitude $A_P$ of mass $P$ is
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** Maximum velocity $V = A\omega$

$v_P = v_Q$

$A_P\omega_P = A_Q\omega_Q$

$\frac{A_Q}{A_P} = \frac{\omega_P}{\omega_Q}$ $\left(\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}\right)$

$= \sqrt{\frac{k_p}{m_p} \frac{m_q}{k_q}}$

$= \sqrt{\frac{k_1}{k_2}}$

questions.stem_en: The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes $\text{n} = 2 \rightarrow \text{n} = 3$ and $\text{n} = 4 \rightarrow \text{n} = 6$ transitions, respectively, is
questions.stem_ta: [NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes $\text{n} = 2 \rightarrow \text{n} = 3$ and $\text{n} = 4 \rightarrow \text{n} = 6$ transitions, respectively, is
questions.explanation_en:
$$\Delta\text{E} = \frac{\text{hc}}{\lambda} = \text{E}_{\text{final}} - \text{E}_{\text{initial}} \quad \left(\text{E}_{\text{n}} = \frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{\text{n}^2}\right)$$

$$\Delta\text{E}_{2\rightarrow 3} = \frac{\text{hc}}{\lambda_{2\rightarrow 3}} = \text{E}_3 - \text{E}_2 = \frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{3^2} - \left(\frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{2^2}\right)$$
$= \text{R}_{\text{H}} \left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right)$
$= \text{R}_{\text{H}} \times \frac{5}{36}$

$\therefore \lambda_{2\rightarrow 3} = \frac{\text{hc} \cdot 36}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 5}$

$$\Delta\text{E}_{4\rightarrow 6} = \text{E}_6 - \text{E}_4 = \frac{-\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{36} + \frac{\text{R}_{\text{H}}}{16} = \frac{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \times 20}{36 \times 16}$$

$\frac{\text{hc}}{\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6}} = \frac{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \times 20}{36 \times 16}$

$\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6} = \frac{\text{hc} \times 36 \times 16}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 20}$

$$\frac{\lambda_{2\rightarrow 3}}{\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6}} = \frac{\frac{\text{hc} \cdot 36}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 5}}{\frac{\text{hc} \times 36 \times 16}{\text{R}_{\text{H}} \cdot 20}}$$
$= \frac{1}{4}$

questions.stem_en:
Energy and radius of first Bohr orbit of $\text{He}^+$ and $\text{Li}^{2+}$ are

[Given $\text{R}_\text{H} = 2.18 \times 10^{-18}\text{ J}, \text{a}_0 = 52.9\text{ pm}$]
questions.stem_ta:
[NEET 2025 அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வினா — Chemistry: Chemistry NCERT Core] Energy and radius of first Bohr orbit of $\text{He}^+$ and $\text{Li}^{2+}$ are

[Given $\text{R}_\text{H} = 2.18 \times 10^{-18}\text{ J}, \text{a}_0 = 52.9\text{ pm}$]
questions.explanation_en:
**Sol.** $\text{E}_\text{n} = \frac{-2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \text{z}^2}{\text{n}^2}\text{ J}; \text{r}_\text{n} = \frac{52.9 \times \text{n}^2}{\text{z}}\text{ pm}$

For $\text{He}^+$

$\text{E}_{\text{He}^+} = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times 4 = -8.72 \times 10^{-18}\text{ J}$

$\text{r}_{\text{He}^+} = \frac{52.9 \times 1}{2} = 26.45\text{ pm}$
